limits.text: 01Helix is nonclinical: not a diagnostic, variant classification or medical advice tool. ClinVar's classification is shown as a database record with its review status, not as advice.

02The curated sets of this build are FAAH2 and HBB; other genes are refused rather than built from uncurated data. This set (FAAH2) carries the gene, its MANE Select transcript and sequences, the protein record and a predicted model (listed, not loaded).

03No experimental structure is curated for FAAH2: no experimental structure is cross-referenced for this protein. There is no Protein World, no residue mapping and no variant placement in this set; Helix shows the transcript, its sequence and the protein record, and never substitutes a predicted model.
04The data are a snapshot of public records with a retrieval date and record versions (see Evidence World), not a live feed. Records change between builds.
05The DNA helix is illustrative geometry: the bases, their order and the exons are real, the shape and spacing are not to scale.
06The AlphaFold model of Q6GMR7 (AF-Q6GMR7-F1) is listed as a computational prediction; it is not loaded and is never shown as an experimental structure.

07A language model, when one is available, only proposes a plan of fixed actions; deterministic code checks every identifier and executes. Its wording is never a scientific claim. Its suggested next questions are shown only when a fixed filter finds them nonclinical and answerable with the curated data. Without a model, a rule-based planner answers a limited set of questions.
08Evidence World v1 is a page layer, not yet a world the planner can enter: the plan vocabulary has no evidence world, and adding one would change the Phase 3 prompt.
09Tested in headless Chrome on one Mac. Safari, Firefox and the desktop webview were not run in this phase.
